neurips-2024-self-distilled-depth-refine.tldr: SDDR uses self-distilled depth edges and Poisson-style fusion to refine noisy depth maps.
paragraphs: Depth refinement should turn coarse predictions into detailed maps with sharp boundaries. Patch-merging methods can be inefficient and inconsistent, and existing refiners often blur edges. This paper models those problems as noisy Poisson fusion with local inconsistency and edge-deformation noise.

Self-distilled Depth Refinement, or SDDR, creates cleaner depth-edge pseudo-labels through coarse-to-fine self-distillation. Edge-guided gradient and fusion losses then optimize refinement in a form equivalent to Poisson fusion. As depth predictions improve, the pseudo-labels also become less noisy.

Across five benchmarks, the method improves accuracy, edge quality, efficiency, and generalization. Training another model directly with SDDR-generated edge labels also helps. The abstract does not provide metric values or runtime comparisons. The contribution is a coupled edge-labeling and refinement process, with evidence that its learned supervision can transfer beyond the original refinement model.

neurips-2024-sprinql-sub-optimal-demonst.tldr: SPRINQL learns from expert and suboptimal demonstrations while weighting their influence differently.
paragraphs: Offline imitation learning often has few expert demonstrations but many lower-quality trajectories. Ignoring the latter wastes coverage, while copying them indiscriminately can teach poor behavior. SPRINQL aims to use both sources without losing the expert target.

The method builds on inverse soft-Q learning and assigns learned weights that emphasize agreement with expert demonstrations more strongly than agreement with suboptimal ones. A central theoretical contribution reformulates the offline imitation objective as convex optimization over the space of Q functions.

Comprehensive benchmark experiments report state-of-the-art offline-imitation performance. The abstract does not give scores or establish that every parameterized implementation retains convexity. Its contribution is a weighted learning formulation for mixed-quality demonstrations; the healthcare and human-robot examples motivate the setting but are not themselves reported as validated deployments in the supplied abstract.

neurips-2024-statistical-computational-t.tldr: Density-estimation data structures face a near-linear tradeoff between query samples and search time.
paragraphs: The paper studies selecting a distribution close to an unknown query distribution from a collection of k known distributions over n outcomes. A data structure must balance how many query samples it needs, how long selection takes, and how much information it stores.

For a broad class of polynomial-space data structures, using O(n/log^c(k)) samples forces query time at least k^(1-O(1)/log log(k)). This is close to linear in the number of candidates. The lower bound holds even when the query exactly equals a candidate and every candidate is uniform on half the domain.

The authors also construct a simple data structure matching the lower-bound instance asymptotically and show practical efficiency experimentally. The result limits the analyzed data-structure class; it should not be read as excluding every specialized method under additional assumptions about a particular distribution collection.

neurips-2024-tight-rates-for-bandit-cont.tldr: Bandit control reaches optimal square-root regret for smooth strongly convex costs beyond the quadratic case.
paragraphs: Control problems with adversarial disturbances and only bandit feedback are harder than standard linear-quadratic settings. Nonquadratic costs and dependence on previous actions complicate gradient estimation. This paper asks whether optimal regret remains possible under smooth, strongly convex costs.

The proposed algorithm reduces nonstochastic bandit control to bandit convex optimization without memory, avoiding the memory obstacle in the usual reduction. It combines this change with recent techniques for general strongly convex bandit optimization.

The resulting regret is roughly O(sqrt(T)), improving the previous O(T^(2/3)) rate up to logarithmic factors and matching the optimal order for the studied setting. An improved bandit-convex-optimization algorithm with memory is an additional contribution. The abstract does not report experiments or extend the guarantee to arbitrary nonsmooth, nonconvex costs; the smoothness and strong-convexity requirements are central.

neurips-2024-uda-a-benchmark-suite-for-r.tldr: UDA benchmarks retrieval-augmented question answering on lengthy, unstructured real-world documents.
paragraphs: Retrieval-augmented generation must handle more than clean text passages in practical document analysis. Academic and financial material often combines prose and tables in lengthy HTML or PDF files. UDA creates a benchmark for evaluating that more complicated setting.

The Unstructured Document Analysis suite contains 2,965 real-world documents and 29,590 expert-annotated question-answer pairs. The authors revisit language-model and retrieval-augmented solutions across multiple document domains and query types, examining design choices as well as answer quality.

The findings emphasize the importance of parsing and retrieval. The abstract does not give individual system rankings, scores, or a universally best pipeline, so those details require the linked benchmark paper. The contribution is a shared evaluation resource and comparative analysis that can expose failures before answer generation, where table extraction or passage selection may already have lost the required evidence.

neurips-2024-understanding-and-improving.tldr: Optimization analysis explains weaknesses of training-free diffusion guidance and motivates improvements.
paragraphs: Training-free diffusion guidance uses existing networks trained on clean data to steer generation toward a desired loss. It offers flexible control without training a new conditional generator, but its behavior differs from classifier-based and classifier-free guidance.

This paper analyzes the procedure from an optimization perspective. It shows that training-free guidance is more vulnerable to misaligned gradients and can converge more slowly than classifier guidance. Those findings explain why reusing an off-the-shelf predictor does not automatically produce equally effective guidance.

The authors propose several techniques to address the limitations, with theoretical rationale and experiments in image and motion generation. The abstract does not describe each technique or provide numerical gains. Its contribution is a clearer account of the optimization challenges plus supported remedies, rather than the claim that all training-free guidance methods share one performance level or eliminate the need for careful objective design.

neurips-2024-united-we-stand-divided-we-.tldr: ADV-TRA uses adversarial trajectories as more robust fingerprints of neural-network behavior.
paragraphs: Model fingerprinting seeks to identify copied neural networks without modifying them. Fingerprints based on isolated inputs can be fragile when decision boundaries change and may falsely resemble unrelated models. ADV-TRA uses sequences of progressively adversarial inputs to capture a richer behavioral signature.

The trajectory design tolerates larger changes in the decision boundary. A surface-trajectory construction combines fixed-length trajectories with dynamically adjusted step sizes, aiming to make fingerprints distinctive while keeping query costs relatively low.

Experiments on three datasets against four types of removal attack distinguish copied and unrelated models better than state-of-the-art comparisons. The abstract does not provide false-positive rates or query counts. The contribution is a more robust behavioral identification scheme; a fingerprint match is evidence within the tested threat model, not by itself a complete legal determination of ownership or infringement.

neurips-2024-units-a-unified-multi-task-.tldr: UniTS uses task tokens and shared representations to support multiple time-series objectives.
paragraphs: Time-series models are often specialized for forecasting, classification, anomaly detection, or imputation. UniTS brings predictive and generative tasks into one framework through task tokenization and a modified Transformer block designed for shared time-series representations.

Pretraining draws on heterogeneous domains with different dynamics, sampling rates, and time scales. The aim is to transfer a common model to downstream datasets with differing task specifications rather than train unrelated architectures for each objective.

Evaluation spans 38 datasets in human activity, healthcare, engineering, and finance. Comparisons include 12 forecasting, 20 classification, 18 anomaly-detection, and 16 imputation models, with superior reported performance and strong few-shot and prompting capabilities. The abstract does not provide per-dataset metrics. Its evidence supports broad multitask usefulness in the tested collection, including competitive single-task settings, without claiming one model dominates every possible time-series application.

neurips-2024-watch-out-for-your-agents-i.tldr: Agent backdoors can target intermediate behavior even when the final answer appears correct.
paragraphs: Language-model agents interact with tools and external environments, creating attack surfaces beyond the initial prompt and final response. This paper formalizes backdoor threats for agents and distinguishes different places where triggers and malicious behavior can occur.

One attack category changes the final output; another alters an intermediate reasoning step while leaving the final output correct. Triggers can appear in a user query or in an observation returned by the environment. These distinctions make final-answer inspection alone an incomplete evaluation of agent behavior.

Experiments on web-shopping and tool-use tasks find substantial vulnerability, with existing textual-backdoor defenses offering limited mitigation. The abstract does not report attack-success rates or a new effective defense. The contribution is a threat framework and empirical assessment showing why security evaluations should examine the agent’s full interaction process, within the tested backdoor settings.

neurips-2025-a-circular-argument-does-ro.tldr: Spherical RoPE questions whether positional equivariance is necessary for strong vision-model learning.
paragraphs: Rotary positional encodings are often credited for their relative, equivariant treatment of positions. This paper first characterizes that mathematical property, showing RoPE as a highly general equivariant solution in one dimension and Mixed RoPE as the corresponding multidimensional solution under commuting generators.

The authors then relax equivariance by introducing Spherical RoPE with anticommuting generators. This provides a comparison that changes the structural condition often assumed essential to rotary positional encoding while retaining an analogous construction.

Empirically, Spherical RoPE exhibits learning behavior equivalent to its equivariant counterparts. The authors interpret this as evidence that relative-position structure may be less necessary than commonly believed. The abstract gives no benchmark scores or universal equivalence theorem for performance. Its theoretical characterization and empirical challenge should be distinguished: the latter suggests design freedom, rather than proving equivariance never matters.

neurips-2025-a-pre-training-framework-fo.tldr: Task Vector Estimation pretrains relational models with schema-aware predictions of future dynamics.
paragraphs: Relational-database tasks differ through table structure, temporal relationships, and the logic defining their labels. A generic pretraining objective may overlook information important for a downstream task. Task Vector Estimation, or TVE, builds task-relevant structure into pretraining.

TVE creates supervisory signals through set-based aggregation over schema-traversal graphs and explicitly models dynamics in the next time window. An information-theoretic analysis argues that task-informed representations preserve more relevant signal than representations learned without those priors.

Experiments on RelBench consistently outperform traditional pretraining baselines. The abstract does not identify each task or report numerical gains, and the theoretical result depends on how task information enters the model. The contribution is a relational pretraining design that treats schema, label-generation structure, and time as central modeling choices rather than assuming all downstream database tasks are interchangeable.

neurips-2025-accurately-predicting-prote.tldr: H3-DDG models multiscale many-body interactions to predict mutation effects on protein binding.
paragraphs: Predicting how mutations change binding free energy requires capturing interactions that extend beyond isolated residues. H3-DDG uses a hypergraph-driven hierarchical network to model higher-order, many-body effects at multiple scales, connecting local changes with global protein interactions.

On SKEMPI v2, the method reaches a Pearson correlation of 0.75 and reports a 12.10% improvement in multipoint-mutation prediction. On BindingGYM, it outperforms Prompt-DDG and BA-DDG by 62.61% and 34.26%, respectively, although the abstract does not specify the metric underlying those relative improvements.

Ablation and efficiency analyses support robustness and scalability, and a SARS-CoV-2 antibody case study illustrates potential affinity-design applications. The abstract does not establish clinical effectiveness or experimental validation of every predicted mutation. Its contribution is a structured interaction model with benchmark evidence and a focused design case study.

neurips-2025-admtree-compressing-lengthy.tldr: AdmTree compresses long contexts through information-aware segments arranged in a semantic tree.
paragraphs: Long contexts make Transformer attention expensive, but compressing them can discard local details or weaken long-range relationships. AdmTree aims to preserve both fine-grained content and global coherence through adaptive hierarchical compression.

The framework segments text according to information density and summarizes variable-length segments with gist tokens. These become leaves of a semantic binary tree, combined by a lightweight aggregation mechanism. The backbone language model stays frozen, limiting the number of additional trainable parameters.

The abstract describes intended advantages including reduced positional bias, content-adaptive compression, and stronger semantic preservation. It does not report benchmark datasets, quantitative quality results, or measured speedups. The supported contribution is therefore the architecture and its design rationale; the extent to which it preserves every important detail or improves practical long-context performance requires evidence from the full paper.

neurips-2025-autojudge-judge-decoding-wi.tldr: AutoJudge accelerates speculative decoding by learning which token mismatches matter for answer quality.
paragraphs: Speculative decoding usually preserves the target model’s output distribution token by token. AutoJudge relaxes that requirement in a task-specific way, accepting some draft-model mismatches when they are unlikely to harm the completed answer.

A semigreedy search identifies which mismatches should be corrected, producing supervision without human annotation. A lightweight classifier built on existing language-model embeddings learns to make those acceptance decisions during inference. The method is deliberately lossy, exchanging a small quality reduction for additional speed.

On GSM8K with Llama 3.1 70B, it achieves up to roughly 2x speedup over speculative decoding with at most a 1% accuracy drop. On LiveCodeBench, it accepts at least 25 tokens per speculation cycle with about a 2% Pass@1 reduction. These are task-specific measured tradeoffs, not a distribution-preserving or zero-quality-loss guarantee.

neurips-2025-barista-brain-scale-informe.tldr: BaRISTA shows that spatial tokenization scale matters when pretraining models of intracranial brain activity.
paragraphs: Intracranial recordings capture interactions across individual channels and larger brain regions. Transformer models must decide how that spatial structure becomes tokens and which units to mask during self-supervision. BaRISTA provides a framework for studying those design choices.

The model is a spatiotemporal Transformer trained through masked latent reconstruction, with flexible spatial scales for both encoding and masking. This lets the authors compare channel-level representations with larger regional groupings while keeping the broad learning framework consistent.

On public multiregional intracranial electrophysiology data, both choices substantially affect downstream decoding. Larger-than-channel spatial encodings improve decoding, and regional tokens still support accurate channel-level reconstruction. The abstract gives no numerical gains or clinical outcome evidence. Its contribution is a scale-aware modeling framework and empirical evidence that common channel-level tokenization is not necessarily the strongest choice for these recordings.

neurips-2025-beyond-benign-overfitting-i.tldr: A classical interpolating estimator exhibits several distinct generalization regimes as one parameter changes.
paragraphs: Fitting noisy training data exactly does not always produce poor test performance. This paper revisits the interpolating Nadaraya–Watson estimator, also called Shepard’s method, to study generalization beyond a simple distinction between statistical consistency and inconsistency.

By varying one bandwidth-like hyperparameter, the authors prove the existence of catastrophic, benign, and tempered overfitting regimes. Their order changes nonmonotonically, showing that even a classical estimator can have a subtle relationship between interpolation and prediction error.

Numerical experiments reproduce the theoretical phenomena. The analysis also suggests that, for tuning this parameter, overestimating intrinsic data dimension is less harmful than underestimating it. The abstract does not provide exact regime boundaries or error formulas. The result concerns this estimator and its assumptions, rather than establishing that overparameterized neural networks follow precisely the same transitions.

neurips-2025-can-dpo-learn-diverse-human.tldr: A finite-training analysis links DPO generalization to the diversity of preferences and available samples.
paragraphs: Preference optimization must account for people with different values, not only one uniform notion of a good response. This paper develops a theoretical framework for direct preference optimization that asks how generalization changes with value diversity and training-sample quantity.

The analysis follows each sample’s reward margin over a finite number of gradient steps, reflecting training that stops before an idealized infinite-time limit. From those trajectories, the authors derive a generalization-error bound that exposes the difficulty of learning a broad collection of concepts or values.

Experiments with contemporary language models validate the theory’s relevance. The abstract does not give the explicit scaling formula or numerical findings, so it does not establish a universal sample count sufficient for alignment. Its contribution is a framework for analyzing diversity and finite optimization together, rather than assuming strong average preference performance guarantees representation of everyone’s values.

neurips-2025-causalvtg-towards-robust-vi.tldr: CausalVTG addresses dataset shortcuts and absent queries in video temporal localization.
paragraphs: Video temporal grounding locates the segment matching a language query. Systems can exploit superficial object-word correlations and often assume a matching segment must exist. CausalVTG targets both limitations, including cases where the requested event is absent.

A causality-aware disentangled encoder uses front-door adjustment to reduce confounding in visual and textual representations. A multiscale temporal module reconstructs query-conditioned features at several resolutions, while a counterfactual contrastive objective teaches the model to assess whether the query is grounded at all.

Across five benchmarks, the method improves localization at stricter intersection-over-union thresholds and more accurately identifies genuine query-video matches. The abstract does not provide numerical scores or the assumptions supporting its causal interpretation. The evidence supports the combined architecture on those evaluations, rather than proving all dataset-induced bias has been removed.

neurips-2025-ccl-causal-aware-in-context.tldr: CCL selects in-context examples through learned causal features to improve transfer across distributions.
paragraphs: Choosing demonstrations that resemble a query can help in-context learning, but superficial similarity may fail when source and target data differ. Causal-aware In-context Learning, or CCL, aims to select examples using features expected to remain meaningful under distribution shift.

The method uses a variational-autoencoder-based causal representation technique to represent the dataset and query. Demonstrations are then chosen according to similarity in those learned causal features, rather than relying only on conventional feature resemblance.

The authors provide theoretical and empirical evidence of improved out-of-distribution generalization for language models. The abstract does not specify datasets, numerical gains, or the identifiability assumptions of its causal representation. Its contribution is a demonstration-selection strategy motivated by invariance, with supporting evaluations; it does not establish that arbitrary latent features learned without sufficient assumptions are necessarily causal.

neurips-2025-chiqpm-calibrated-hierarchi.tldr: CHiQPM combines hierarchical explanations with calibrated prediction sets while retaining high point accuracy.
paragraphs: An interpretable classifier should explain its overall decision structure and individual predictions. CHiQPM combines global contrastive explanations with a hierarchy that users can traverse, aiming to make both the model’s classes and its uncertainty easier to understand.

The hierarchy supports an interpretable conformal-prediction procedure that returns coherent sets along the explanation structure. This extends the model beyond a single class label, while retaining local and global interpretability within the same system.

The evaluation reports state-of-the-art point prediction while retaining 99% of the accuracy of noninterpretable models. That means relative accuracy retention, not necessarily a 99% classification accuracy. Calibrated set predictions are competitively efficient against other conformal methods. The abstract does not give dataset-level results or user-study evidence, so improved human-AI collaboration is a proposed benefit rather than a directly quantified outcome here.

neurips-2025-conservative-classifiers-do.tldr: Learning theory changes when classified people genuinely improve rather than merely manipulate their features.
paragraphs: Strategic classification often assumes people alter their presentation to obtain favorable decisions. This paper studies a different response: agents genuinely improve. It characterizes learning when such improvement possibilities interact with the classifier, extending earlier results that found unexpectedly favorable generalization behavior.

An asymmetric version of minimally consistent concept classes yields an exact characterization of proper learning in the realizable setting. The authors also study Euclidean-ball improvement sets and characterize improper learning under a generative assumption on the data distribution.

Further results address bounded-noise models and mistake bounds for realizable and agnostic online learning, resolving earlier open questions. The abstract does not provide explicit bound formulas or empirical tests. Its contribution is a set of assumption-dependent learnability characterizations, not evidence that every real person responds constructively to automated decisions or that conservative classification is universally desirable.

neurips-2025-contextual-dynamic-pricing-.tldr: Contextual pricing learns heterogeneous buyer types with near-optimal dependence on time and feature dimension.
paragraphs: A seller setting prices repeatedly may observe contextual features and only whether a purchase occurred. This paper allows buyers to have different valuation types drawn from an unknown distribution with finite support, rather than assuming one homogeneous population.

The proposed contextual pricing algorithm uses optimistic posterior sampling. If the type distribution has support size K-star and the context dimension is d, its regret is roughly O(K-star sqrt(dT)), up to logarithmic factors. The authors prove the dependence on d and the horizon T is tight to that precision.

For the noncontextual case, a variance-aware zooming algorithm improves the analysis to achieve optimal dependence on the number of types. The abstract does not report experiments or describe all valuation assumptions. The results are theoretical pricing guarantees within this heterogeneous finite-type model, not a universal revenue guarantee for unrestricted customer behavior.

neurips-2025-dualfocus-depth-from-focus-.tldr: DualFocus constrains spatial and focal behavior to distinguish depth edges from texture artifacts.
paragraphs: Depth-from-focus estimates geometry from images captured at different focus settings. Fine textures and abrupt depth changes can create ambiguous cues, making it difficult to tell a real depth boundary from an appearance pattern. DualFocus uses the gradient structure of the entire focal stack.

The framework introduces dual variational constraints. Spatial constraints compare how gradients change across focus levels to separate depth edges from texture. Focal constraints enforce unimodal, monotonic focus probabilities consistent with the expected physical behavior of focusing.

Experiments on four public datasets outperform state-of-the-art comparisons in both depth accuracy and perceptual quality. The abstract does not provide numerical errors or specify failure conditions. Its contribution is a task-specific combination of spatial and focal inductive biases, with empirical support in difficult regions rather than a guarantee that all ambiguous focus stacks uniquely determine scene depth.

neurips-2025-efficient-large-language-mo.tldr: Neural Block Linearization replaces selected attention layers with estimated linear maps without fine-tuning.
paragraphs: Language-model attention is expensive at inference, but some layers may be well approximated by simpler computations. Neural Block Linearization, or NBL, estimates linear replacements using linear minimum-mean-squared-error estimators and selects where they are likely to cause the least distortion.

Canonical correlation analysis provides a theoretical upper bound on approximation error. The method uses that bound to choose attention layers for substitution and applies directly to pretrained models without additional fine-tuning.

Across reasoning benchmarks, NBL speeds inference while retaining competitive accuracy. Replacing 12 attention layers in DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Llama-8B increases inference speed by 32% with less than a 1% accuracy tradeoff. The abstract does not specify the runtime hardware or every task metric. The result supports selective approximation in the tested model, not unrestricted replacement of all attention computations without quality loss.

neurips-2025-empowering-decision-trees-v.tldr: Shape Generalized Trees use visualizable nonlinear feature functions to make compact decision trees.
paragraphs: Ordinary decision trees often need many simple threshold splits to represent nonlinear feature effects, producing deep structures that are hard to inspect. Shape Generalized Trees replace each internal split with a learnable axis-aligned shape function acting on one feature.

Users can visualize these functions to understand the node’s decision mechanism. The authors introduce ShapeCART to learn the trees, then extend the framework to bivariate shape functions and multiway branching with corresponding induction algorithms.

Experiments across multiple datasets show improved predictive performance with smaller models than traditional axis-aligned linear trees. The abstract does not provide accuracy values, tree sizes, or measured human-comprehension results. Its contribution is a richer but still visualizable branching representation, with empirical evidence that nonlinear decisions at individual nodes can reduce the amount of tree structure needed for the evaluated tasks.
